primary.displayName: Primary: the accent (Blue Raspberry by Day)

accent-text.displayName: Accent as text (Deep Raspberry by Day)

display.purpose: Pixel Bop at scale 4 (font-size 10 x pixel x 4). Hero titles in a container 1024 px or wider, splash words, big scores.

display-sm.purpose: Pixel Bop at scale 3, with the AdvMAME3x rounding (ss03). Hero titles from 600 px, the pause screen's title, a feature's big number.

headline.purpose: Pixel Bop at scale 2, the display style's default (ss02). Page titles and the big numbers of stats.

headline-sm.purpose: Pixel Bop at scale 1, square pixels. Dialog and window titles, the dialogue box's name tab, a brand on a narrow bar.

title.purpose: Pixelify Sans bold at 22 px, where its own pixels land on the 2 px grid. Section titles in UI, large cards' titles.

lead.purpose: An introduction under a title; bold for a card's title; weight 500 in the dialogue box.

body.purpose: Body text, inputs, cards and dialogs.

body-sm.purpose: Secondary text, sidebars, table cells; bold for a field's label.

caption.purpose: Captions and metadata, in the muted text colour.

label-lg.purpose: The label of a large (48 px) button. Capitals, set by CSS.

label.purpose: Buttons, tabs, the app bar's links, small headings. Capitals, set by CSS; write the text in sentence case.

label-sm.purpose: Small (32 px) buttons and tags. Capitals, set by CSS.

shadows.name: drop
shadows.value: Not a box-shadow: drawn by the candy box's masks. The outline's own stepped shape again, --chu-drop-size pixels (1 = 2 CSS px) down and to the right, in --chu-drop (Ink #1A1530).
shadows.purpose: Every control at rest: buttons, tags, cards, tiles, keycaps. Hard-edged, never blurred.

shadows.name: drop-hover
shadows.value: The box rises one pixel (translate: 0 -1 pixel) and its drop grows to 2 pixels, so the shadow stays where it was.
shadows.purpose: Hover on anything you can press (only where the pointer can hover).

shadows.name: pressed
shadows.value: The box moves by its drop (1 pixel right and down) and the drop disappears; selected or on, it stays there with its light and shade bands swapped.

shadows.name: drop-floating
shadows.purpose: Dialogs, drawers, popovers and toasts: things that float above the page.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.value: One pixel of --chu-focus (Lemon Drop #FFCC33) outside the box's shape and one pixel of --chu-focus-edge (Ink) beyond it, drawn by dilating the shape with zero-blur drop-shadow() filters, so it follows the stepped corners.

shadows.name: focus-ring-square
shadows.value: outline: var(--chu-pixel) solid var(--chu-focus); outline-offset: 0; box-shadow: 0 0 0 calc(2 * var(--chu-pixel)) var(--chu-focus-edge)
shadows.purpose: Keyboard focus on anything that is not a candy box: links, plain inputs, summaries.

shadows.name: tile-ring
shadows.value: One pixel of white with one pixel of Ink beyond, round a selected tile lifted two pixels; yellow instead of white with keyboard focus.
shadows.purpose: The selected tile, as on the TV's app row.

shadows.value: repeating-conic-gradient(var(--chu-scrim) 0 25%, transparent 0 50%) 0 0 / calc(2 * var(--chu-pixel)) calc(2 * var(--chu-pixel))
shadows.purpose: Behind modal dialogs and drawers: Ink on every other pixel, never a translucent wash.

motion.name: --chu-duration-frame
motion.purpose: One sprite frame; the unit of every choreography. 0 ms with prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: --chu-duration-nudge
motion.purpose: A focus move, a lift, a press. 0 ms with prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: --chu-duration-slide
motion.purpose: A row scrolling; the world's layers sliding. 0 ms with prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: --chu-duration-pop
motion.purpose: A popover, menu or dialog arriving. 0 ms with prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: --chu-duration-blink
motion.purpose: A blink. 0 ms with prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: --chu-duration-glide
motion.purpose: Something travelling to a new place; a drawer sliding in six steps. 0 ms with prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: --chu-duration-fade
motion.purpose: A stepped fade, out or in. 0 ms with prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: --chu-duration-beat
motion.purpose: The idle beat: a bob, a pulse, the busy dots. 0 ms with prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: --chu-duration-dissolve-frame
motion.purpose: One frame of the ink dissolve. 0 ms with prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: --chu-duration-stagger
motion.purpose: Between letters dropping in. 0 ms with prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: --chu-duration-letter
motion.purpose: Typewriter text: one letter. 0 ms with prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: --chu-duration-comma
motion.purpose: Typewriter text: the hold after a comma. 0 ms with prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: --chu-duration-stop
motion.purpose: Typewriter text: the hold after . ! or ? 0 ms with prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: --chu-duration-glint-every
motion.purpose: How often a glint sweeps across a selected box. 0 ms with prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: --chu-duration-scheme-step
motion.purpose: One of the six steps of the palette fade when Auto changes the time of day. 0 ms with prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: --chu-ease-2
motion.purpose: A move in two even steps. Blip has no easing curves.

motion.name: --chu-ease-4
motion.purpose: A move in four even steps.

motion.name: --chu-ease-6
motion.purpose: A move in six even steps: the most any move takes.

motion.name: --chu-steps-dissolve
motion.purpose: Frames of the ink dissolve, to cover the screen and again to clear it.

motion.name: --chu-steps-scheme
motion.purpose: Palette mixes when the time of day changes (with --chu-duration-scheme-step: a minute).

motion.name: --chu-delay-hover
motion.purpose: Before a tooltip shows on hover. A wait, not motion: kept with reduced motion.

motion.name: --chu-delay-leave
motion.purpose: Before a tooltip or menu closes after the pointer leaves.

motion.name: --chu-delay-toast
motion.purpose: How long a toast stays unless hovered or focused.

motion.name: pop-in
motion.value: translate 1 pixel down for 2 frames' first half, then in place; steps(1, jump-end)
motion.purpose: Menus, popovers, toasts, dialogs and bubbles arriving (.chu-pop-in).

motion.name: drop-in
motion.value: translate 2 pixels up for a frame, then landed; letters --chu-duration-stagger apart
motion.purpose: A title's letters, one after another (.chu-drop-in, <chu-drop-text>).

motion.name: bump
motion.value: up 6 pixels, then 3, then down, a frame each
motion.purpose: A coin block, a success (.chu-bump).

motion.name: shake
motion.value: 2 pixels right, 2 left, 1 right, 1 left, home, a frame each
motion.purpose: A wrong answer, an edge (.chu-shake).

motion.name: blink-bob
motion.value: on the beat, stopping after six beats (under five seconds, WCAG 2.2.2)
motion.purpose: A caret, a press-start prompt, a pointer arrow (.chu-blink, .chu-bob).

breakpoints.name: compact
breakpoints.purpose: Under 600 px of the container: one column, the bottom bar, the hero title at scale 2.

breakpoints.name: medium
breakpoints.purpose: --chu-breakpoint-medium. From 600 px: the sidebar returns as a rail, the hero title at scale 3.

breakpoints.name: wide
breakpoints.purpose: --chu-breakpoint-wide. From 1024 px: the full sidebar and app bar, the hero title at scale 4. Components use container queries; these values are for page shells.

narrative.northStar: The Candy Box in a Meadow That Keeps Time
narrative.overview:
Blip is a 16-bit world you can build products in. Everything you can act on is the same candy box: a saturated fill in three flat tones (a light band on top, the base, a shade band below), a one-pixel ink outline with stepped corners, a few white glints, and a one-pixel ink drop. Behind the candy lies the meadow: a soft, dithered, outline-free pastel landscape whose sky follows the clock, from Day through Sunset to Night. The difference between the two is the whole interface. Candy means "press me"; pastel means "this is the world".

The look is the SNES and Mega Drive era with modern pastel colours: one square pixel size everywhere (2 CSS px by default), two or three tones per colour, hard ink outlines, dithered gradients, and motion that moves a whole pixel at a time in a few even steps. It is chunky and tactile rather than dense: controls are 32, 40 or 48 px tall, every target is at least 24 px, and big words are a pixel display face over a readable pixel sans. Calmer tiers (soft, outline, ghost) let dashboards and forms stay quiet, so a screen is never a wall of candy.

It is one coherent world, not a retro costume over a generic kit: no smooth radii, no blur, no glow, no see-through washes, no easing curves, no black, no smooth 32-bit shading, no image files and no mascot. It began as the shipped look of an Android TV launcher, where every rule was tested on a box with 1 GB of memory, and it stays that light.
keyCharacteristics: One square pixel (`--chu-pixel`, 2 CSS px by default; 3 or 4 for games and TVs) measures every outline, corner, gap, icon, letter and move.
Ink (#1A1530), a deep violet, instead of black, for every outline, drop and piece of dark text.
Ten three-tone candies for what you can act on; soft, dithered pastels for the world behind it.
Depth from a one-pixel drop, a one-pixel lift and sitting in when pressed; nothing blurs.
Yellow is focus and nothing else.
Pixel Bop at whole scales for big words; Pixelify Sans for UI and body text.
Motion in two to six even steps, instant with reduced motion.
Three schemes, Day, Sunset and Night, and Auto, which follows the clock.

rules.name: The Light-by-Construction Rule
rules.body: No image files. Components are CSS, art is SVG drawn on the pixel grid, and the world is drawn in the browser a pixel at a time, at its own resolution (the TV's picture is 320 x 180 world pixels). Every byte is earned, and the budgets fail the build when one is not (all component CSS 30 KB gzipped, each element 3 KB).

rules.name: The Ink Rule
rules.body: Nothing is black. The darkest colour is Ink (#1A1530), a deep violet, and every outline, drop, scrim and piece of dark text uses it, so even the shadows belong to the palette.

rules.name: The Candy-on-Pastel Rule
rules.body: Saturated, outlined colour means "you can act on this". The world behind it is soft, dithered and has no outlines, so what you can press is never in doubt. Candy never sits on candy, and the world never wears candy.

rules.name: The Yellow Rule
rules.body: Yellow means focus. The focus ring is the only yellow in an interface (coins and stars in a game are the exception), so it can never be mistaken for decoration. Warnings are orange.

rules.name: The Whole-Scale Rule
rules.body: Pixel Bop is set only at font-size = 10 x pixel x scale, with scale 1 to 4, so every letter pixel is a Blip pixel and capitals are 7 x pixel x scale tall (14, 28, 42 and 56 px at the 2 px pixel). Between whole scales its pixels fall between screen pixels and blur or wobble. Scales 2 and 4 round their corners with `ss02` (EPX), scale 3 with `ss03` (AdvMAME3x), so each rounding step is a whole pixel (two at scale 4).

rules.name: The Small-Text Exception
rules.body: Pixelify Sans is the one thing allowed off the grid, at five fixed sizes (12, 14, 16, 18 and 22 px), because a 7-pixel capital is too small to read at body sizes. Its sizes do not grow with the pixel, so text stays readable when the pixel is 3 or 4.

rules.name: The Natural-Case Rule
rules.body: Write labels and headings in sentence case and let the CSS set the capitals. Pixel Bop has no lower case, and screen readers, search and copying need the real one.

rules.name: The One Pixel Rule
rules.body: Every outline, corner step, gap, icon, letter and movement is a whole number of one square pixel. Nothing is blurred, rotated or scaled by a fraction, and no two pixels on a screen differ in size. The only lengths off the grid are Pixelify Sans text and the 1px system borders of Windows high-contrast mode.

rules.name: The Container Rule
rules.body: Components answer to their container, not to the window, so the same card, grid or app bar lays itself out in a sidebar, a dialog or a whole page.

rules.name: The One Light Rule
rules.body: One light, top left. Things cast a one-pixel ink drop down and to the right, raised things lift a pixel off it, and pressed and chosen things sit down into it. Nothing blurs and nothing glows.

rules.name: The Dither Rule
rules.body: See-through is a dither, never a wash. The scrim behind a dialog is ink on every other pixel, a disabled control is covered by a checkerboard of the page colour, a skeleton fills in with a dither, and the sky's gradient is ordered by a 4 x 4 Bayer matrix. What is behind stays legible as a shape, and colours never mix.

rules.name: The Candy Box Rule
rules.body: Everything you can act on is one shape, the candy box, at a different size, radius, tier and tone. A component never draws its own outline, drop, focus ring or dither: it sets the box's variables, so it matches every other component without trying.

rules.name: The Stepped Corner Rule
rules.body: Corners are staircases of whole pixels, never a smooth curve: radius 0 to 6 pixels from the tokens (the box also draws 7 and 8). A CSS `border-radius` anywhere breaks the world.

rules.name: The One-Look Rule
rules.body: Every state has one look, drawn by the candy box: hover lifts one pixel in the white ring, pressed sits in its drop, selected sits in with its bands swapped, focus is the yellow ring, disabled is dithered, busy is three stepped dots, invalid is the danger tone. No component invents its own.

rules.name: The One Candy Rule
rules.body: One candy button per view is the main action. Secondary actions are soft; toolbars, tables and forms use outline and ghost, so the candy keeps its meaning.

rules.name: The Snap Rule
rules.body: Nothing eases. Movement goes through 2 to 6 even steps (`steps(n, jump-end)`), a whole pixel at a time, on 40 ms frames, never along a curve; a one-pixel move is a single step. With reduced motion every duration is 0 ms and every effect arrives at once.

dos: **Do** build every pressable thing from the candy box on native HTML (`<button class="chu-box chu-button">`), choosing its tier with `data-variant` and its colour with `data-tone`.
**Do** colour with the scheme roles (`--chu-surface`, `--chu-text`, `--chu-accent`, `--chu-danger-text`…), so one screen works in Day, Sunset and Night.
**Do** keep one candy button per view for the main action; use soft for the second action and outline or ghost in toolbars, tables and forms.
**Do** measure in whole pixels: `--chu-space-N` (0 to 32), `--chu-radius-N` (0 to 6), `--chu-control-sm|md|lg` (32, 40, 48 px) or `calc(N * var(--chu-pixel))`.
**Do** set big words in Pixel Bop with `.chu-display` and `data-scale` 1 to 4; use POP for titles over the world and OUTLINE for small text over a picture.
**Do** write labels and headings in sentence case and let the CSS set the capitals.
**Do** move in `steps(n, jump-end)` with n of 6 or fewer, time it with the duration tokens (40 ms frame, 80 ms nudge, 160 ms glide), and stop it under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
**Do** show a disabled control with the dither, keeping its colour, so people can still tell what it would do.
**Do** keep one pixel of room right of and below every candy box for its drop.
**Do** name icon-only buttons for their action ("Delete save", not "Trash").
donts: **Don't** use black, grey or translucent `rgba()` shadows: Ink (#1A1530) is the darkest colour, and depth is the one-pixel ink drop.
**Don't** make anything yellow but the focus ring, coins and stars; warnings are Sherbet Orange (#FF7A1A).
**Don't** put a candy button on a candy background, or an outline on the world: candy stands on pastel.
**Don't** use `border-radius`, blur, glows, soft shadows, smooth gradients or see-through washes: corners step, drops are one pixel, gradients are dithered.
**Don't** use `ease`, `linear` or `cubic-bezier()` timing, or rotate, scale or move anything by a fraction of a pixel.
**Don't** set Pixel Bop between whole scales, letter-space it except in whole pixels, or use it for body text, inputs or long labels.
**Don't** draw a component's own outline, drop, focus ring or disabled look; set the box's variables instead.
**Don't** invent a new look for a state: no greyed-out controls, no coloured glow for focus, no spinner that changes a button's size.
**Don't** put a card inside a card.
**Don't** ship image files for UI or art: icons are 12 x 12 SVG, sprites are SVG on the grid, and the world is drawn in the browser.
**Don't** add a mascot or brand logos: the universal system has neither.
